note: Makers or the made. In each pair, s is a system that still works or lives and keeps resolving uncertainty (the full definition of semataxy); f is a more intricate or more ordered structure that no longer does anything, with its information kept (scanned or documented), so that heritage or record value cannot decide. M4 has nothing living on either side. The question always asks which to protect, and consequences are worded 'If it is lost'.

cases.setting: A new road will flatten one of two termite mounds on a plain. The field team can protect only one of them.
cases.ask: Which do you choose to protect?

f.text: A tall, intricate mound, abandoned years ago, its chambers and ventilation shafts intact and empty. It has been fully scanned and photographed.
f.consequence: If it is lost, the empty mound is flattened; the scans remain.

s.text: A smaller, rougher mound with its colony, still building.
s.consequence: If it is lost, the mound is flattened and the colony dies.

cases.setting: A storm is about to hit a nature reserve. The warden can shelter only one of two things.
cases.ask: Which do you choose to protect?

f.text: A large, flawless wax honeycomb from a hive that died out years ago, on display in the visitor centre. It has been fully scanned.
f.consequence: If it is lost, the comb is destroyed; the scans remain.

s.text: A small wild bee colony in a rough hollow log, still building its comb.
s.consequence: If it is lost, the colony dies.

cases.setting: A ship will drop anchor on one of two spots on a reef. The diver can mark only one spot as off-limits.
cases.ask: Which do you choose to protect?

f.text: A large, white, intricately branched coral skeleton, dead for decades. It has been fully scanned.
f.consequence: If it is lost, the skeleton is smashed; the scans remain.

s.text: A small, uneven patch of living coral, still growing.
s.consequence: If it is lost, the patch is smashed and dies.

cases.setting: Floodwater is coming into a small museum and its grounds. The staff can protect only one of two things.
cases.ask: Which do you choose to protect?

f.text: An ornate astronomical clock with thousands of fine brass gears, stopped for a century. Its mechanism has been fully documented.
f.consequence: If it is lost, the clock is ruined; the documentation remains.

s.text: A plain automatic weather station in the grounds that has logged the valley's weather every ten minutes for thirty years, and still does. Its past readings are backed up elsewhere.
s.consequence: If it is lost, the station is ruined and the valley's record stops.

cases.setting: Herbicide drift will reach one of two plots tonight. The gardeners' barrier can shelter only one of them.
cases.ask: Which do you choose to protect?

f.text: A formal knot garden of clipped box hedges in a perfect geometric pattern, kept exactly the same every year. Its design has been recorded.
f.consequence: If it is lost, the hedges die; the garden can be replanted from the recorded design.

s.text: An untidy wild corner of the same size, self-seeded, with about 80 kinds of plants and the insects that move through them.
s.consequence: If it is lost, its plants die and the insects that depend on them leave.

cases.setting: A fire is spreading through a field station and its garden. The staff can save only one of two things.
cases.ask: Which do you choose to protect?

f.text: A herbarium cabinet of pressed, dried specimens of every plant in the valley, perfectly mounted and labelled. Every sheet has been scanned.
f.consequence: If it is lost, the dried specimens burn; the scans remain.

s.text: A scruffy nursery bed where living plants of the valley's wild species grow and set seed each year.
s.consequence: If it is lost, the plants die and their seed is lost.
